# Remove-ZbxAction

## SYNOPSIS

Removes actions.

## SYNTAX

```
Remove-ZbxAction [-InputObject] <ZabbixReference<ZabbixAction>[]> [-Force] [-Connection <ZabbixConnection>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

An action reacts to events: when its conditions match a trigger, discovery, autoregistration, internal or service event, it sends messages, runs scripts or changes hosts. The Remove-ZbxAction cmdlet deletes the actions given to -InputObject (names, ids or piped objects) with action.delete, all in one call when the pipeline ends. It asks for confirmation first unless -Confirm:$false or -Force is given, and -WhatIf lists what would be deleted. It writes nothing, and needs a connection made with Connect-ZbxServer.

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Delete an action

```powershell
Remove-ZbxAction -InputObject 'Notify on disaster' -Confirm:$false
```

Deletes the action Notify on disaster. -Confirm:$false skips the prompt the command shows by default.

### Example 2: Preview deleting the actions a search finds

```powershell
Get-ZbxAction -Name 'Notify*' | Remove-ZbxAction -WhatIf
```

Lists the actions whose names start with Notify that the command would delete, and deletes nothing.

## INPUTS

- `ZabbixReference<ZabbixAction>[]`: Bound to -InputObject (ByValue). Represents a reference to an API object: a parameter that points at an API object takes its id, its name, or the object itself piped from a Get- cmdlet, and becomes an id before the call — one parameter, three spellings, one resolution.
